text:
[LTAC.5.3] A missed tick — when the engine is paused, sleeping,
or otherwise unable to evaluate during a scheduled tick — must
not skip the timer firing. The follow-up rule's LHS uses
`monotonic_ns() >= t.fire_at`, which holds on every later tick; the
follow-up fires late, never lost. The guard is `>=` against an
absolute instant rather than equality against a scheduled one,
and that is the whole mechanism — an equality test would lose
exactly the tick this clause is about.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__due
idris.note: `>=` against the absolute instant `fire_at`, not equality against a scheduled tick: the mechanism, as the test.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__due_edges
idris.note: The first tick whose sample reaches `fire_at`, at or past it. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__due_edges_total
idris.note: One firing exactly when some tick reaches `fire_at`: never lost.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__edges_are_first_due
idris.note: The edge is at the first tick to reach `fire_at`, however many samples were skipped.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick
idris.note: A missed tick does not skip the firing: the next tick at or after `fire_at` fires.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__due_rising
idris.note: `>=` holds on every later tick once it holds: the guard cannot be missed.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__late_edge
idris.note: A tick that lands past `fire_at` still fires the follow-up: late, not lost.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__lte_lte_b
idris.note: What the `>=` is, as a Bool of the clock.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__missed_tick_fires_late
idris.note: The tick at 2 is missed; the tick at 3 fires. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__missed_tick_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the missed tick. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__never_lost
idris.note: Over any history, the follow-up fires late and never lost: exactly once when the clock has reached `fire_at`.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__never_lost_is_an_instance
idris.note: NEVER LOST at the one-shot history: the counts sum to one, the final clock having reached `fire_at`. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__once_if
idris.note: Fired late or not at all, never twice: the count a history sums to. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_expr
idris.note: `>=` against the absolute instant, as the clause requires, written on the `dwell` leaf. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_4__guard_is_due
idris.note: `>=` against the absolute instant `stamp + dur`, carried through: what the `dwell` guard decides is what the clause's guard decides.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick_timed
idris.note: A missed tick does not skip the firing: the next tick at or after `fire_at` fires, on this engine.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__lte_is_lte_b
idris.note: The two Boolean orders on naturals -- the Prelude's `lte`, which the `dwell` gate uses, and Rete/TmsRun.idr's `lte_b`, which Rete/NetworkAfter.idr's gate uses -- are one function. By induction.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__never_lost_timed
idris.note: NEVER LOST, on the Idris model's engine: over any tick history from a clock below the stamp plus the duration, the follow-up has fired exactly once when the history's final clock has reached it, whatever ticks were missed on the way, and not at all when it has not.

idris.name: rtim_3_2_6__one_move_timed
idris.note: A move that lands past `fire_at` still fires the follow-up: late, not lost. Executed.
